wtp_range.note: Expressed monthly for comparability; sold as INR 199/yr or INR 49/season. The idea's INR 20/month list price sits between target and aspirational. FX ~INR 88/USD (estimate).

van_westendorp.derivation: too_cheap 0: alerts are free everywhere; post-application info is free on Telegram/YouTube/TrueJobs. cheap_but_acceptable INR 8 (~INR 99/yr): impulse-annual level in Indian edtech promos. getting_expensive: modal competitor price is INR 0; anchored to ~20% of the nearest paid bundle (Testbook ~INR 749/yr = ~INR 62/mo -> INR 12.5) x desire multiplier 1.32 = ~INR 16.5/mo. Cross-check vs Indian utility analogues: Truecaller ad-free ~INR 39/mo or INR 399/yr and Premium INR 75-99/mo for a DAILY utility; JioHotstar Mobile INR 79/mo or INR 149/quarter for daily entertainment. An event-driven govt-job tool should sit well below those -> INR 16-25. too_expensive INR 40 (~INR 499/yr): ~2/3 of a full mock-test pass, and Truecaller ad-free monthly level.

desire_premium_rationale: Primary control (1.2-1.5x); label moderate -> low end 1.2x; secondary survival scores 4 -> +10% => 1.32. Same as v1. On a ~zero base the premium is a few rupees.
recommended_pricing_model: Freemium (no ads; matched alerts + persistent reminders free) -> Pro as (a) INR 199/yr auto-renewing via Play Billing/UPI AutoPay and (b) INR 49 non-renewing 'season pass' (prepaid, ~90 days around an application window). Lead with the season pass at the moment of 'Mark as applied' — that is when the lifecycle value becomes concrete. Strongly consider bundling one human/automated pre-submit Form Check (Form Pakka's paid unit) into the season pass, because that is the only step with observed WTP.

pricing_models_considered.fit_rationale: Aspirants apply year-round across exams; annual fits multi-year prep.
pricing_models_considered.risk: India D35 download-to-paid ~0.7%; event-driven use gives weak felt value between events; UPI AutoPay sees ~20M revocations/month for low balance.

pricing_models_considered.fit_rationale: Matches cash-flow and episodic need; Google Play supports prepaid subscriptions in India; quarter passes normal (JioHotstar INR 149/qtr).
pricing_models_considered.risk: No recurring revenue; must re-sell each season; INR 49 net ~INR 41 after Play fee.

pricing_models_considered.fit_rationale: Only observed WTP in the category (cafés INR 30-150/form).
pricing_models_considered.risk: Human-review ops; liability; a service, not an app.
Destroys the 'quiet, trustworthy' core promise; CPC ~$0.01 means tiny yield.
Monthly churn + payment friction; INR 20 x 0.85 = INR 17 net — Play/UPI failure rates make monthly the worst option.

recommended_price.launch_tactic: Founding-member 2-year pass INR 349 capped at 500 buyers (cash + reviews only).

net_after_store_fee.note: Google Play 15% service fee on subscriptions (estimate; UPI/Razorpay web checkout ~2% would net more but loses in-app convenience).

freemium_conversion_rationale: Base: framework 'utility' typical 1-4% is US-calibrated; India/SEA download-to-paid ~0.7% (RevenueCat via secondary sources). Truecaller — India's most successful utility subscription — has ~2M India subscribers on a user base reported at ~350M (unverified), i.e. ~0.6%, for a daily-use product. v2 improvements over v1's 0.8%: (1) no ads, so the free tier is good — that cuts both ways; (2) clear value gate at 'Mark as applied' (free stops at applying; Pro tracks what comes next), which is better gating than v1's 'ad-free/WhatsApp'; (3) a INR 49 sachet lowers the barrier. Estimate 1.2% of installs (~2.5-4% of users who mark at least one application as applied). Kept below 2% because desire is moderate, the pain is episodic, and free substitutes cover post-application news. UNVALIDATED — no product in the category shows paying users.

competitive_pricing_range.notes: Alerts and trackers: INR 0 (modal). India Govt Job Finder lists $2.99/mo / $4.99/yr IAP (iOS, contradictory listing; no evidence of payers). Max = Testbook pass ~INR 56-62/mo equivalent. Transactional: cafés INR 30-150/form.

category_benchmark_range.india_adjusted_note: Target ~$0.18/mo is far below the framework's $1 minimum -> per skill rule 'may struggle to sustain development'. Truecaller India's ~$0.50-1.10/mo is the realistic Indian utility ceiling for a daily product.

b2b2c_potential.rationale: Speculative: verified structured eligibility feed licensed to coaching institutes, café/CSC operators or edtechs (INR ~2,000-10,000/mo, no evidence). The structured-rules database built for matching is the asset most likely to have B2B value. Future only.

pro_unit_costs.note: Fallback channels are affordable for payers only; offering them free would cost more than the free tier earns.

market_insights_pricing_signals: pro-tier-economics: Truecaller ~2M India subs (daily utility) -> sub-1% paid share even for the best Indian utility
pro-tier-economics: JioHotstar Mobile INR 79/mo, 149/qtr, 499/yr -> sachet/quarter norms
pro-tier-economics: UPI AutoPay mandates doubling YoY but ~20M revocations/month on low balance
pro-tier-economics: WhatsApp utility ~INR 0.12-0.15/msg -> Pro delivery margin OK
pricing_rationale: v2 fixes the v1 pricing logic problem (what does Pro sell?) with a coherent loss-avoidance bundle gated at the right moment ('Mark as applied'), and INR 199/yr + INR 49 season pass are sensible Indian price points. It does NOT fix the evidence problem: monetization_evidence for paid govt-job utilities is still empty — no competitor visibly earns subscription revenue, and the one with listed IAP contradicts itself. Pricing remains UNVALIDATED. The INR 16-20/mo target means even at 3% conversion revenue per install is ~INR 5/yr. The single highest-leverage pricing move is to put a pre-submit Form Check inside the season pass, attaching Pro to the one step aspirants already pay for.
